source: A Night Off design doc p. 10 (Conversation), p. 26 (Dialogue: text with gibberish voices, captioned; drunk captions substitute the spoken line), p. 40 (conversation math). Lines are ours; the doc asks for about 40 per regular in the end (stage 7).

ask: What's the story with you, then?
joke: A squid walks into a bar. Eight arms, no tip.
I'd tell you a joke about the Nautilus, but it'd go over your head. Underneath it, actually.
My captain says I drink like a fish. Fish drink water. Checkmate.
Why did the crab never share? He was shellfish.
challenge: Bet you can't back that up.
drunk_agree: You're my best friend. Who are you?
drunk_joke: Why did the... the thing... HA. I forget. HA.
Knock knock. No wait, I'M the door.
drunk_challenge: Your face is a hull with barnacles on.
I could take you. I could take anyone. Hold my drink. Hold me.

Talker: Oh! Sit, sit. Have I told you about my knee?
Hustler: You've got the look of someone who's good at pool.
Gambler: Got any money? Asking for a friend.
Sailor: Nautilus, eh? Bet my lot drinks yours under the table.
Oddball: The gulls are talking tonight. Did you hear?
Have you ever counted the bubbles in a pint?

ask_ok: Most people don't ask. Here's the thing.
joke_ok: HA! Oh, that's terrible. Tell another.
That's the worst thing I've heard all week. I love it.
joke_fail: I've heard better from the goat.
challenge_ok: Ha! You've got some brass. I like that.
challenge_fail: Say that again. I dare you.
You want to take this outside?
listen: ...so I says to him, I says...
...and that was the year of the eels...
...which is why I don't trust lighthouses...
end_good: Here, let me tell you something nobody knows...

laugh.text: A laugh shared: +5 charisma for 5 minutes

flirt._source: doc p. 13 (the flirt mini-game: open with a compliment, a joke, a drink or a dance; build with four options; the offer; signals), p. 14 (the kidney thieves are the best flirts, and their lines are the funniest)

compliment: That colour's doing things for this whole room.
You've the best laugh in the Gull, and I've heard them all.
Has anyone told you you're the only interesting thing here?
joke: A squid walks into a bar. Eight drinks, no hands free.
I'd tell you a joke about the tide, but it'll come back to you.
What did the ocean say to the sailor? Nothing. It waved.
drink: Whatever they're having, and one for me.
Let me get this one. And the next.
dance: The jukebox is playing our song. It's playing everyone's song.
Come on, one turn round the floor.
ask: What's the best night you've had in here?
Where'd you learn to smile like that?
lean: You know, I almost didn't come out tonight.
It's loud in here. Lean closer.

drunk: Your eyes are like two... no, wait, I've lost it.
I love you. I love everyone. Where's my drink?
Do you want to see my anchor? It's a tattoo. Mostly.
I could lift that table. Watch. No. Don't watch.
My ship's called the Nautilus. Do you like submarines? I LIKE submarines.

joke: Ha! That's terrible. Tell me another.
I'm laughing against my better judgement.
You're an idiot. I like idiots.
drink: You know the way to my heart.
A gentleman sailor. Rare as pearls.
dance: You're treading on my feet, and I don't mind.
ask: Oh, you don't want to hear all that. Well, if you insist...
That's a long story. Have you got all night?
lean: I've a feeling about you, too.

compliment: Is that a line? It sounded like a line.
Hm. You say that to everyone.
I've heard better from the dog.
drink: I'm not that easy. Or that thirsty.
dance: Ask me after another drink. Yours, not mine.
ask: Why do you want to know?

thief_ok: Oh, you're funny. I could just take you home and keep you.
You've the healthiest glow in the room. I mean it as a compliment.
Do you drink much? No reason. I just like a sailor who looks after himself.
Has anyone ever told you you've beautiful insides?

tells.married: turns a ring on their finger
tells.sweet: pours you a water from the jug

decline: Another night, then. You're good company.
Shame. Stay and have one more, at least.
Your loss, sailor. I'll be here.
end_bad: I think I'll find someone else to talk to.

items: a matchbook from the Brass Monkey
